# #4602: Patch: the Infinite Assault, CF, the card foundation (IA-25 to IA-240)
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

Part of #4601, the cards' fullsend tree (and of the tracker #4576). **CF, the card foundation**: every shared row of
the Infinite Assault's cards IA-25 to IA-240 and their 13 tokens, with a stub script per entry, so the card parts
C2 to C10 each touch only their own scripts and build side by side. It lands first; every card part waits on it.

The plan of record is [`docs/infinite-assault.md`](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/claude/gallant-ritchie-pwshvk/docs/infinite-assault.md): on `main` once C1 (#4577) merges, and until then on the planning branch `claude/gallant-ritchie-pwshvk`. Where it and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins (CLAUDE.md). Read its IA11 and IA12 whole, and `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` first (CLAUDE.md rule 10): its "A card of a set
that has not shipped" says what a held set's foundation writes, as Training Grounds' foundation (#2194) and
Stinkyscape+'s (#3535) did. C1 (#4577) has already put the set's row, its hold, its tags, its census entry, its
scripts folder, §8.13's heading and IA-1 to IA-24 on `main`, which this tree's branch is cut from.

## Build

1. **Every catalog entry** of IA-25 to IA-240 and the tokens IA-25.1, IA-34.1, IA-35.1, IA-40.1, IA-41.1,
   IA-74.1, IA-78.1, IA-82.1, IA-143.1, IA-154.1, IA-200.1, IA-216.1 and IA-235.1, after C1's entries in
   number order: both faces (cost, type, rarity, stats, keywords, text with `{key}` where a number is a
   `param`, the `read` marks, `dealsDamage`), the `AI` tag and its doctrine's tag, `Commander` on IA-217 to
   IA-240, and a `flavor` in the set's voice (IA11's fiction). `loc` is the stub's until its card part writes
   the script.
2. **A stub script per entry** in `crates/cards/src/scripts/infinite_assault/cNNN_slug.rs`: its `pub const ID`,
   its header comment quoting its §8.13 text with `STUB (#4602):`, and a `pub fn script()` that does nothing yet,
   as #2194's stubs did.
3. **Every table the tests demand, once:** the census's counts and tags, the fixture rows, `docs/radiant-audit.md`'s
   rows (each verdict against R275 is yours), `card-text.yaml` (flavour, voice lines, Chinese), `card-audio.json5`,
   the FX table's lines, and §8.13's rows in `spec/08-catalog.md` under C1's heading, each as the plan words it,
   corrected where the engine's vocabulary or R275 asks (say so in the row's part's issue with a comment).
4. **The verbs the set lacks.** Read every card against §6 and list, in a comment on this tree's parent, each
   verb, keyword, filter or board fact a card needs that the engine has not, with the cards that need it, so the
   card parts and the reconcile know where engine work lands.

## Done when

- All 229 entries, their stubs and every per-entry table are written; `cargo test --workspace --features
  jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts` passes with the set held; `cargo jackioh catalog check`,
  `spec check` and `names --check` pass; `golden check` and `fuzz --seeds 200` are unchanged.
- The census counts the set as IA11's table does (82, 64, 50, 30 and 14 by rarity, C1's 24 included).
- The comment listing the missing verbs is on #4601.

## The design rules (IA11)

**The design rules every card part keeps.**

1. **Real cards.** Each card is legal in an ordinary game and plays the same in any mode; none reads the
   mode or its level. Commons to Legendaries of the doctrines and the Core sit on JackiOh's curve (costs
   (0) to (4); about 4 stats at (1), 8 at (2), 12 at (3), 16 at (4) for a Unit with little text, less with
   more), so they can be reused. Commander cards are boss cards, above the curve on purpose.
2. **Spicy, never unfair.** Swingy and rule-bending is the point, but every threat has an answer the player
   can see coming: a countdown is shown, a wall can be killed, a bluff can be called. Nothing makes the
   player lose with no counterplay, and nothing locks them out of playing for a turn they can't foresee
   (Kill Switch, IA-140, fires on a third card, which the player may choose not to play).
3. **Expressible.** The text uses verbs, keywords and filters the engine has (§6); where a card needs a new
   one, its part adds it by `docs/ADDING_CARDS.md` §6, with its test. Numbers are `params` (`{damage}`),
   never literals (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
4. **Radiant is about twice the base face** (R275): doubled stats and a better line, never stats alone for
   a Unit with text. Each part writes its `docs/radiant-audit.md` rows.
5. **"Infinite Assault card"** in a card's text is a pool that names the set, which reaches the set while
   it is held (R1846001: a pool that names its set keeps to it). "Created" is the engine's Created mark.
6. **The AI must pilot it.** A card whose prompt the AI can't answer well is fixed or redesigned in its
   part, not shipped hoping.
7. **The part may tune.** A part may change a number, a word or a Radiant line where the engine or balance
   asks, keeping the card's role and its spice, and says so in its pull request; a bigger change goes in a
   ruling note.
